slides.title: Alibaba Launches Qwen-Robot Series Embodied AI Large Models
slides.tldr: ALIBABA RELEASES QWEN-ROBOT EMBODIED AI MODELS
slides.highlight: Alibaba has launched the Qwen-Robot series of embodied AI large models, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated learning.

slides.title: Evaluating Large Language Models Abilities for Addressee, Turn-change, and Next Speaker Prediction in Meetings
slides.highlight: This research evaluates LLMs and multimodal LLMs on addressee detection and speaker prediction, contributing to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and engagement in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: LLMs outperform humans and supervised models in next speaker prediction for multi-party meetings using conversational context.
card.key_idea: A unified framework evaluating addressee detection, turn-change, and next speaker prediction across supervised models, text-based LLMs, MM-LLMs, and humans using the AMI corpus.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the AMI Meeting Corpus using accuracy and F1 scores; compared supervised baselines, Qwen3, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and 12 human subjects.
card.limitation: Human evaluation was conducted by non-native English speakers, potentially underestimating baseline human performance.

slides.title: Generating Natural and Expressive Robot Gestures through Iterative Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback using LLMs
slides.highlight: This research uses ChatGPT and iterative reinforcement learning with human feedback to create more fluid and expressive co-speech gestures for the Pepper humanoid robot, advancing human-robot interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Iterative RLHF improves the expressiveness and fluidity of LLM-generated co-speech gestures for the Pepper robot.
card.key_idea: Combines GPT-4 with a low-level motion primitive library, using Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and few-shot prompting to refine gestures based on iterative human ratings.
card.evaluation: Five-round online user study (250 participants) rating 50 phrases. Results showed statistically significant improvements (p<0.001) in expressiveness, relevance, and fluidity.
card.limitation: Relying on low-level primitives can lead to mode collapse, repetitive patterns, and difficulty sustaining gesture diversity.

slides.title: MuVAP: Multimodal Multiparty Voice Activity Projection for Turn-taking Prediction in the Wild
slides.highlight: MuVAP uses a single camera and monaural audio to predict speaker-aware turn-taking in multiparty interactions, supporting HyECHO's goals in multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: MuVAP predicts multiparty turn-taking using a single camera and monaural audio via role-relative projections.
card.key_idea: A causal framework grounding acoustic projections in face tracks, using Role-Relative Projection to map N-speaker dynamics onto a fixed current-versus-next floor-holder state for scalability.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the new 31-hour AVCC dataset using Shift-Hold (Macro-F1) and Next-Speaker Prediction (Accuracy) tasks; outperformed MLP and unimodal baselines.
card.limitation: Performance is lower in 'Active' prediction tasks compared to 'Silent' ones, and 3-speaker settings are more challenging than 2-speaker scenarios.

slides.title: WaveSync: Constrained Wavefront Optimization for Synchronized Co-Speech Gestures in Humanoid Robots
slides.tldr: SYNCHRONIZED CO-SPEECH GESTURES FOR HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: WaveSync uses a hybrid framework and LLM-driven semantic importance waves to synchronize expressive gestures with speech while ensuring kinematic feasibility. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: WaveSync synchronizes humanoid robot gestures with speech emphasis while respecting strict physical kinematic constraints.
card.key_idea: An LLM generates a Semantic Importance Wave; Dynamic Movement Primitives shape trajectories, and a wavefront optimizer aligns gesture peaks to speech peaks via duration compression and forward propagation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via PyBullet simulations across five scenarios using objective metrics (HbS, PAM, Jerk) and subjective Likert ratings from 20 participants; outperformed three ablated baselines.
card.limitation: Relies on a fixed action library, limiting its ability to handle unconstrained dialogue; not yet tested on physical hardware.

slides.title: Beyond Usability: A UX Case Study on Using "Withdrawal Design" to Challenge Engagement Metrics in Social Robotics
slides.tldr: CHALLENGING ENGAGEMENT METRICS IN SOCIAL ROBOTICS
slides.highlight: This study examines how the withdrawal of a social robot can prompt children with autism to seek human interaction, suggesting that high engagement may sometimes silo social behavior. It is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Withdrawal of social robots may better promote human interaction than continuous robot engagement for autistic children.
card.key_idea: A mixed-methods randomized controlled trial comparing continued robot use versus robot withdrawal to evaluate effects on social motivation and human-centric interaction.
card.evaluation: 8-week home trial (N=40) using SCARED, RCADS, SMS, RMET, and SUS metrics; results show a trade-off between anxiety reduction and social motivation.
card.limitation: High robot usability may mask ecological downsides by siloing social behavior within the child-robot dyad.

slides.title: Adaptive Turn-Taking for Real-time Multi-Party Voice Agents
slides.highlight: This work introduces ModeratorLM, which improves turn-taking precision and reduces interruptions in multi-party conversations. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and engagement within hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: ModeratorLM is a role-playing voice agent that adapts turn-taking behavior based on assigned personas in multi-party conversations.
card.key_idea: A streaming speech LLM that conditions turn-taking and responses on explicit roles, featuring a reasoning-augmented variant (ModeratorLM-Think) using chain-of-thought reasoning over conversational context.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on real-world meeting data (NSF-1) and synthetic RolePlayConv dataset; showed >40% precision and >70% recall improvements over non-role-conditioned baselines.
card.limitation: The model relies heavily on textual transcriptions for decisions; performance degrades substantially when transcription is unavailable.

slides.title: A Neuro-Symbolic Approach to Strategy Synthesis for Strategic Logics
slides.highlight: This work introduces a generate-and-certify framework using LLMs as strategy-generation oracles for multi-agent systems, aligning with MIMIC's use of neuro-symbolic and LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: A neuro-symbolic framework using LLMs to synthesize and formally certify strategies for Natural Alternating-time Temporal Logic.
card.key_idea: A generate-and-certify architecture where an LLM proposes candidate natural strategies, which are then formally validated by the VITAMIN NatATL model checker to ensure soundness.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a new 4,211-instance NatATL dataset using Qwen3-32B; achieved 92% accuracy and scaled to 50 states and 11 agents.
card.limitation: Some instances remain undecidable due to token limits (8192), resulting in truncated outputs and parsing errors.

slides.title: Co-Creating Buildable and Open Social Robot Study Companions with University Students
slides.tldr: OPEN-SOURCE SOCIAL ROBOT DESIGN FOR ASSEMBLY
slides.highlight: This research explores how Design for Assembly and Disassembly can lower barriers for students building open-source social robots, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: DfA and DfD mechanical redesigns significantly improve the usability and perceived buildability of open-source social robots.
card.key_idea: Applied the Double Diamond framework to create RSC v4.1, replacing screws with twist-locks, snap-fits, and tool-free latches to reduce assembly friction and improve serviceability.
card.evaluation: Two studies (developers and first-time builders) using SUS, NASA-TLX, and assembly timing. SUS rose from 59.4 to 89.4 for developers; results appear consistent.
card.limitation: Small, non-random samples; potential self-evaluation bias in developers; lack of inter-rater reliability checks for thematic coding.
